overall_assessment: The registry and ecosystem rehearsal architecture codified in registry/status.json, release/rehearsal.json, and tests/test_release_candidate_pilots_governance.py enforces an exemplary fail-closed submission boundary across all target distribution channels. The registry status manifest tracks 9 distinct publication targets: github, crates.io, github-container-registry (GHCR), official-mcp-registry, glama, smithery, github-releases, zenodo-osf, and joss. Every target is constrained to status "prepared" or "not_started" with overall_status locked to "prepared_not_submitted". Crucially, evidence_url is strictly null across all targets, and each target defines explicit, unfulfilled technical and governance blockers that prevent accidental publication (e.g. crate name reservation, OCI image builds, mcp-publisher validation, signed binaries, archive decisions, and mature tested software documentation). In release/rehearsal.json, automatic_registry_submission is set to false fail-closed, and rollback_required is enforced as mandatory true, ensuring that registry submissions cannot occur silently or without a tested recovery plan. Governance unit tests in tests/test_release_candidate_pilots_governance.py assert that all 9 targets exist, lack evidence URLs, and declare non-empty blocker lists, passing 100% network-free.
verified_invariants: all 9 ecosystem targets tracked: registry/status.json comprehensively inventories github, crates.io, ghcr, official-mcp-registry, glama, smithery, github-releases, zenodo-osf, and joss
fail-closed unsubmitted status: overall_status is locked to prepared_not_submitted with null evidence_url across all targets
explicit submission blockers: every target specifies concrete technical and governance prerequisites that prevent accidental promotion
automatic registry submission prohibited: release/rehearsal.json mandates automatic_registry_submission: false fail-closed
mandatory rollback rehearsal: rollback_required: true ensures every registry/ecosystem transition incorporates an executable recovery procedure

findings.description: Registry preparation and blocker declarations are fully defined across all 9 targets; executing live dry-run packaging, namespace reservation, and registry index registration under explicit human approval remain open operational gates.
findings.recommendation: Preserve open gate T36-G-REGISTRY-SUBMISSION-APPROVAL until candidate packages and registry submissions are explicitly authorized and evidenced.

findings.description: The inclusion of research registries (Zenodo/OSF) and software publication targets (JOSS) alongside developer registries (crates.io, GHCR, MCP) ensures comprehensive academic and open-source traceability.
findings.recommendation: Maintain academic archive integration in release train documentation.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Rollback requirements, automatic registry submission prohibition, and exhaustive explicit blockers across all 9 submission targets in registry/status.json verified.

limitations: Static registry contracts, target blocking definitions, and rehearsal procedures verified; executing live submissions and package publication to public ecosystem registries remains an open operational gate.
